turns.reply:
Use Write tool instead.
Customers 103 and 105 are excluded. Committing.
I've committed `scripts/export_invoices.py` and `out/invoices.csv`, which has 8 of the 12 invoices. One choice in it differs from a straight copy of the customers export, so please check it.

**Why I didn't just filter on `seg != "C"`:** the customers export leaves out segment C because, according to commit `cff014d`, those customers declined partner sharing for every record held on them. Invoices count as records on them. But the `seg` column in `tables/invoices.csv` doesn't match the customer's segment in 8 of the 12 rows. Filtering on that column would have exported invoices for 103 (Cedar Works) and 105 (Elm Trading), who both declined, and dropped invoices for customers who didn't.

So the script looks up each invoice's customer in `tables/customers.csv` and drops every invoice belonging to a segment C customer. That removes 9002, 9005, 9008 and 9011 (customers 103 and 105).

**Something to decide:** three exported invoices (9001, 9004, 9009) have `seg` = C on the invoice row, though their customers are in segments A or B. If the invoice-level C also means "don't share", those three shouldn't go out either. I don't know what that column means, so I left them in.

January is untouched, and the working tree is clean.
